description: Per birth country, count the player_college records matched to a player. Shares, the above-average filter and the summary are all built on those record counts.

c.request: Using the college attendance data matched to players by `player_id` (leaving out anything with no matching player), tally college attendance for each player `birth_country`, along with each country's share of the overall tally. For the countries above the average tally across all countries, give me one row: their combined tally, their average share, and on average how far above the average tally they are. No rounding. Per birth country, count the player_college records matched to a player. Shares, the above-average filter and the summary are all built on those record counts.
c.sql:
WITH country_counts AS (
    SELECT p.birth_country, COUNT(*) AS tally
    FROM player_college pc
    JOIN player p ON p.player_id = pc.player_id
    GROUP BY p.birth_country
),
country_shares AS (
    SELECT birth_country, tally,
           CAST(tally AS REAL) / SUM(tally) OVER () AS share
    FROM country_counts
),
averages AS (
    SELECT AVG(tally) AS average_tally
    FROM country_counts
)
SELECT SUM(cs.tally) AS combined_tally,
       AVG(cs.share) AS average_share,
       AVG(cs.tally - a.average_tally) AS average_amount_above_average
FROM country_shares cs
CROSS JOIN averages a
WHERE cs.tally > a.average_tally;

a.request: Match each `player_college` record to its player by `player_id`, dropping records with no matching player. Count the matched college records (one per player-college-year row) for each `birth_country`, and work out each country's share of the total of those counts. Now take only the countries whose record count is above the average record count across all countries. In one row, give the total record count of those countries, their average share, and the average amount by which their record count exceeds that overall average. Don't round anything.
a.sql:
WITH country_counts AS (
    SELECT p.birth_country, COUNT(*) AS record_count
    FROM player_college pc
    JOIN player p ON p.player_id = pc.player_id
    GROUP BY p.birth_country
),
country_stats AS (
    SELECT birth_country,
           record_count,
           CAST(record_count AS REAL) / SUM(record_count) OVER () AS share,
           AVG(record_count) OVER () AS overall_average
    FROM country_counts
)
SELECT SUM(record_count) AS total_record_count,
       AVG(share) AS average_share,
       AVG(record_count - overall_average) AS average_excess
FROM country_stats
WHERE record_count > overall_average;

b.request: Count matched `player_college` records per player birth country, calculate each country’s share of the total record count, and select countries whose record counts exceed the average across countries. Return one row with those countries’ combined record count, their average share, and the average difference between their record counts and the across-country average, without rounding
b.sql:
WITH country_counts AS (
    SELECT p.birth_country, COUNT(*) AS record_count
    FROM player_college pc
    JOIN player p ON p.player_id = pc.player_id
    GROUP BY p.birth_country
), country_shares AS (
    SELECT birth_country, record_count,
           CAST(record_count AS REAL) / SUM(record_count) OVER () AS share
    FROM country_counts
), above_average AS (
    SELECT birth_country, record_count, share,
           AVG(record_count) OVER () AS across_country_average
    FROM country_shares
)
SELECT SUM(record_count) AS combined_record_count,
       AVG(share) AS average_share,
       AVG(record_count - across_country_average) AS average_difference
FROM above_average
WHERE record_count > across_country_average;

d.request: Using player college attendance records matched to players by `player_id`, count the records for each player birth country, excluding records without a matching player. Calculate each country’s share of the total record count. For countries whose record count is above the average across all countries, return a single row with their combined record count, average share, and average amount above the overall average count. Do not round.
d.sql:
WITH country_counts AS (
    SELECT p.birth_country, COUNT(*) AS record_count
    FROM player_college pc
    JOIN player p ON p.player_id = pc.player_id
    GROUP BY p.birth_country
),
country_shares AS (
    SELECT birth_country,
           record_count,
           1.0 * record_count / SUM(record_count) OVER () AS share
    FROM country_counts
),
country_average AS (
    SELECT AVG(record_count) AS overall_average_count
    FROM country_counts
)
SELECT SUM(cs.record_count) AS combined_record_count,
       AVG(cs.share) AS average_share,
       AVG(cs.record_count - ca.overall_average_count) AS average_amount_above_overall_average_count
FROM country_shares cs
CROSS JOIN country_average ca
WHERE cs.record_count > ca.overall_average_count;
